title: Draft an Executive Summary & Findings
description: Write an executive summary and findings section for a simulated insider threat case.
problemStatement:
**Scenario:** You have completed an investigation into suspected data theft by an employee. Key facts:
- Employee John Smith used company laptop (Item 001) to copy file `customer_db.xlsx` to a USB drive (Item 002, Kingston DataTraveler, serial 4C530001) on Feb 20, 2026, at 14:30 UTC.
- At 14:35 UTC, he sent an email from his corporate account (j.smith@company.com) to a personal Gmail (john.smith1985@gmail.com) with attachment `customer_db.xlsx` (hash: d2e3f...).
- At 14:50 UTC, he ran a file shredder (Eraser.exe) and securely deleted the local copy and wiped free space.
- The USB drive was recovered and found to contain the customer database file.
- His employment contract explicitly prohibits copying customer data to personal devices.

Write:
1. An **Executive Summary** (2‑3 paragraphs) that a non‑technical HR manager can understand.
2. A **Findings** section (at least 5 bullet points) with proper evidence referencing.

Remember to separate fact from opinion. You may state a conclusion in the Executive Summary but keep Findings factual.
hints: Use plain language; explain what the evidence shows, not how you found it.
Reference evidence items in Findings (e.g., Item 001, Item 002).
Include timestamps in a readable format (e.g., Feb 20, 2026, 14:30 UTC).
Executive Summary should give a high‑level narrative of what happened.
expectedOutput: A well‑structured Executive Summary and Findings list.
solutionCode:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
On February 20, 2026, an investigation was launched following concerns that employee John Smith may have transferred sensitive company data to an unauthorized location. Digital forensic analysis of his company‑issued laptop and a recovered USB drive revealed that Mr. Smith copied the customer database file 'customer_db.xlsx' to a personal USB drive and subsequently emailed the same file to his personal Gmail account. He then used a secure deletion tool to attempt to erase evidence of these actions. The USB drive was recovered and still contained the database file. These actions appear to violate company policy regarding data handling.

FINDINGS
- On February 20, 2026, at 14:30 UTC, a Kingston DataTraveler USB drive (serial 4C530001) was connected to the laptop (Item 001). (Source: USBSTOR registry key, Item 001 image).
- The file 'customer_db.xlsx' (SHA‑256: d2e3f...) was copied to that USB drive at 14:31 UTC. (Source: LNK file in Recent Items, Item 001).
- At 14:35 UTC, an email was sent from j.smith@company.com to john.smith1985@gmail.com with 'customer_db.xlsx' as an attachment. (Source: Office 365 message trace, Item 003).
- At 14:50 UTC, the secure deletion tool Eraser.exe was executed, and free space on the laptop was subsequently wiped with zeros. (Source: Prefetch file CCLEANER64.EXE‑... and zero‑filled unallocated clusters, Item 001).
- The USB drive (Item 002) was forensically imaged and found to contain 'customer_db.xlsx' with a matching hash, proving it is the same file. (Source: forensic image of Item 002).
- No evidence was found that the transfer was authorized or for legitimate business purposes.
